quarterly_data.signal: CFO Ken Parks: in Q4 2025 GE Vernova booked orders of $22.2 billion, a 65% increase year-over-year and a book-to-bill ratio of approximately 2x (equipment orders +91%, service orders +22%); backlog expanded to $150 billion, with equipment backlog $64 billion (up approximately $21 billion and 50% year-over-year) and services backlog $86 billion; Q4 revenue increased 2%, adjusted EBITDA grew 6% to $1.2 billion, free cash flow $1.8 billion, cash nearly $9 billion. Full year 2025: $59 billion of orders (up 34%), approximately $38 billion of revenue (up 9%), adjusted EBITDA +46% with margins +210 basis points, free cash flow $3.7 billion; total backlog up over 25% or $31 billion in the year.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 orders $22.2 billion (65%); backlog $150 billion; FY2025 orders $59 billion (34%); FY2025 revenue $38 billion (9%); FY2025 free cash flow $3.7 billion

quarterly_data.signal: 2026 guidance raised to include Prolec GE (11 months of ownership): revenue $44 billion to $45 billion, up from $41 billion to $42 billion; adjusted EBITDA margin 11% to 13% (unchanged); free cash flow between $5 billion and $5.5 billion, up from $4.5 billion to $5 billion. By segment: Power 16% to 18% organic revenue growth driven by gas power with EBITDA margins between 16% and 18%; Electrification revenue $13.5 billion to $14 billion (20% organic growth plus approximately $3 billion from Prolec GE) with EBITDA margin 17% to 19%; Wind organic revenue down low double digits with EBITDA losses of approximately $400 million. 2026 EBITDA expected more second-half weighted, highest in Q4. Q1 2026: Power high single-digit revenue growth at approximately 14% to 15% EBITDA margin; Electrification revenue similar to Q4 2025 including Prolec GE, margin 16% to 17%; positive free cash flow.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 revenue $44 billion to $45 billion (from $41 billion to $42 billion); free cash flow between $5 billion and $5.5 billion (from $4.5 billion to $5 billion); Electrification revenue $13.5 billion to $14 billion

quarterly_data.signal: By-2028 outlook raised to include Prolec GE: at least $56 billion of total revenue by 2028 (up from $52 billion, a low teens CAGR) with 20% adjusted EBITDA margin; cumulative 2025-2028 free cash flow raised by approximately $2 billion to at least $24 billion, which incorporates nearly $1 billion of incremental CapEx from Prolec GE 'to support increased transformer production'; cumulative CapEx and R&D through the period approximately $11 billion. Electrification: approximately $4 billion of incremental revenue from Prolec on top of high teens organic growth, 22% EBITDA margin maintained, no Prolec synergies included. Dividend doubling in 2026; buyback authorization raised to $10 billion from $6 billion; $3.6 billion returned to shareholders in 2025.
quarterly_data.figure: 2028 revenue at least $56 billion (from $52 billion); cumulative free cash flow at least $24 billion; CapEx and R&D approximately $11 billion; nearly $1 billion Prolec GE CapEx for transformer production

quarterly_data.signal: Gas power: 24 gigawatts of new contracts in 4Q '25 alone (6 gigawatts signed in the last 3 weeks of December); gas power equipment backlog plus slot reservation agreements (SRAs) rose from 62 to 83 gigawatts sequentially (backlog 33 to 40 gigawatts, SRAs 29 to 43 gigawatts), primarily on strong U.S. demand plus agreements in the Middle East, Vietnam and Taiwan; the company entered 2025 with 46 gigawatts on contract. Expects approximately 100 gigawatts under contract by end-2026 (split shifting toward 60% orders / 40% SRAs), shipping high teens in gigawatts in 2026 with new contracts north of 30 gigawatts; CEO Scott Strazik: at 100 gigawatts, '29 and '30 will be 'largely sold out', though 'there are still slots available for 2029' as of January 28; framework discussions for '31 to '35 slots are active. Pricing: 'another 10 to 20 points of pricing strength in the SRAs today' versus existing backlog. Q4 booked 41 heavy-duty gas turbines (the largest orders quarter of the year, an increase of more than 70% YoY, including 15 HA units) and 18 aeroderivative units; about 63 aeroderivative orders in 2025. Management does not view smaller turbine makers as competition — they enable earlier power ahead of heavy-duty units and later serve as reliability backup.
quarterly_data.figure: 83 gigawatts under contract (from 62); approximately 100 gigawatts expected in 2026; SRA pricing 10 to 20 points above backlog; 41 heavy-duty gas turbines in Q4

quarterly_data.signal: Gas turbine capacity build: installed over 200 new machines in its factories and added nearly 1,000 new production workers in 2025; plans an incremental 200 machines and over 500 production workers in 2026. Annual production capacity rises to approximately 20 gigawatts starting midyear '26, a 'substantial step-up in gas turbine output in 3Q '26' ('less than 180 days from now'), so more gas turbines ship in the second half of 2026. Invested more than $2 billion in R&D and CapEx in 2025. Commodity costs are largely locked in with suppliers when orders are taken; long-term service contracts carry material escalators.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately 20 gigawatts annual capacity from midyear '26; over 200 new machines and nearly 1,000 production workers added in 2025; 200 machines and over 500 workers planned for 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Electrification: 'over $2 billion of Electrification's orders were signed directly for data centers in '25, more than triple the 24 total'; demand for grid and data center equipment comes from traditional customers globally and hyperscalers, primarily in the U.S. Q4 was the segment's largest order quarter in its history: orders approximately $7.4 billion (+50% YoY, roughly 2.5x revenue) on synchronous condensers, substations partially to support data center growth, and switchgear; North America equipment orders more than doubled and Middle East rose over $1 billion. Segment backlog $35 billion (+$4 billion sequentially, +$11 billion YoY); equipment backlog $31 billion. Q4 revenue +32% (switchgear and HVDC volume and price), EBITDA margin 17.1% (+320 basis points); FY2025 orders +21%, revenue +26%, EBITDA margin 14.9% (+560 basis points).
quarterly_data.figure: data-center orders over $2 billion in 2025 (more than triple prior year); Q4 orders approximately $7.4 billion (50%); segment backlog $35 billion; Q4 EBITDA margin 17.1%

quarterly_data.signal: Transformer and switchgear capacity: in the transformer product line, labor hours were up 39% in 4Q with output increasing more than 50% year-over-year; the company is doubling transformer and switchgear output from '24 to '28, mostly via more shifts and investment. the acquisition of the remaining 50% stake in Prolec GE received all approvals and closes February 2, and GE Vernova expects to issue roughly $2.6 billion of debt in early February as it completes the deal; Prolec GE brings 5 large factories, and CFO Ken Parks said 'Prolec is a provider of distribution transformers, which are a key part of what's going into data centers', with full ownership letting GE Vernova optimize where transformers go around the world. Electrification's addressable market is 'directionally $150 billion' versus about $14 billion of 2026 revenue (~10%); the segment generated about $5 billion of revenue in '22.
quarterly_data.figure: transformer output up more than 50%; transformer and switchgear output doubling '24 to '28; Prolec GE adds 5 large factories; roughly $2.6 billion of debt to be issued at Prolec GE close

quarterly_data.signal: Solid-state transformer: GE Vernova completed production of its first unit; it will be tested and validated over the summer at a new testing facility in Upstate New York 'before delivering the completed solution to our hyperscaler customer in the autumn of this year' (customer not named). CEO Scott Strazik: it 'could be a substantial order for us with a new product line in 2027 for deliveries later in the decade.'
quarterly_data.figure: first solid-state transformer unit completed; hyperscaler delivery in autumn 2026; potential order in 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Equipment backlog margin: added $8 billion of margin dollars to equipment backlog in 2025, more than the prior 2 years combined, with an incremental 6 points of equipment backlog margin (Power +11 points, mainly gas power); expects to add at least $8 billion again in 2026 and at least $22 billion of equipment margin across '23 to '26. Power added about $12 billion of equipment backlog and $9 billion of services backlog in 2025; power services backlog reached $70 billion. Most higher-margin orders placed in '24 and '25 will not deliver until '27 and beyond.
quarterly_data.figure: $8 billion equipment backlog margin added in 2025; at least $8 billion expected in 2026; power services backlog $70 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Nuclear/SMR: building its first SMR at the Darlington site with OPG in Ontario (drove Q4 Power equipment revenue growth); nuclear was a drag on Power's 2025 margins and 2026 is expected to be directionally similar; SMR expected to contribute meaningfully to Power's top line in the next decade. CEO Scott Strazik said it is working very closely with the U.S. administration, is having productive conversations in Sweden and Poland, and is working with governments and 'customer archetypes, including the hyperscalers' on what nuclear can mean for them in the first half of the next decade, but closing will be slower than gas and grid.
